intervals.label: seafloor installation begins
intervals.note: Start of physical installation of the KM3NeT research infrastructure; construction is still ongoing in 2026 as detection units continue to be added.
intervals.quote: In the early morning of 3 December 2015, scientists and engineers started the installation of KM3NeT

intervals.label: ARCA initial core operational
intervals.note: Marks ARCA's transition to a described 'operational' initial array; physics results have been produced with growing partial configurations (ARCA6, ARCA8, ARCA19, ARCA21, and the 2023 21-detection-unit configuration that recorded the KM3-230213A event) since.
intervals.quote: six detection units are now in operation, representing the initial core of the KM3NeT/ARCA neutrino telescope

intervals.label: ORCA first detection unit online
intervals.note: Start of ORCA data-taking; the ORCA6 configuration used in the 2024 oscillation-parameter measurement was reached later.
intervals.quote: On 22 September 2017, after a two day long sea operation, the first detection unit of the ORCA neutrino telescope came online.

quantity.note: Design capacity; 51 of the planned 230 detection units were operating as of the 2026 access date.
quantity.quote: instrumented volume of ARCA is about 1 cubic kilometer in two 'building blocks' of 115 detection units each
At a depth of about 3500 m

quantity.note: Design capacity (one building block, 115 detection units); 42 detection units installed as of 2026-07-08.
quantity.quote: about 7 Megatonnes of seawater will be instrumented

name: KM3NeT
notes: Modelled as a single experiment record, experiment:km3net, covering both the ARCA and ORCA detectors.

Status recorded as 'commissioning' rather than 'active' or 'construction' alone: KM3NeT is simultaneously still being built (new detection units are added in most sea campaigns) and already producing physics results with partial arrays (see results). 'commissioning' is used for the overlapping, non-terminal intervals in which growing sub-arrays take data; a plain 'construction' interval is also recorded and both remain open (end: null).

summary.plain: An experiment using two neutrino telescopes built into the floor of the Mediterranean Sea, one off Sicily and one off France, to catch faint flashes of light from neutrinos arriving from space and from Earth's atmosphere.
summary.technical: KM3NeT: Mediterranean deep-sea Cherenkov neutrino observatory comprising the ARCA (high-energy astrophysical neutrino) and ORCA (atmospheric neutrino oscillation / mass-ordering) detector arrays, operated by the KM3NeT Collaboration. Under construction since December 2015 with progressively larger partial configurations already taking physics data, including the February 2023 KM3-230213A ultra-high-energy neutrino event.

unique_capabilities.note: Quote (km3net.org detector page, spelling as on the page) supports the two detectors, the same technology and the high-energy vs lower-energy split. The atmospheric-neutrino-oscillation purpose of ORCA is from the abstract of arXiv:2408.07015 ("designed to study oscillations of atmospheric neutrinos").
unique_capabilities.quote: ARCA for the detection of high-energy cosmic neutrinos and ORCA for the detection of lower-energy neutrinos. The two detectors are build with the same technology, but differ in the granularity of the light sensor module
unique_capabilities.value: Two purpose-built deep-sea Cherenkov arrays sharing the same underlying photosensor technology but tuned to different physics: ARCA for high-energy cosmic neutrinos, ORCA for lower-energy atmospheric neutrino oscillations
